candidates.title: Bid to withhold MI5 information from Heaton Park attack inquests
candidates.summary: The Home Office wants the information withheld when the inquests take place next year
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The Home Office wants the information withheld when the inquests take place next year
candidates.evidence_text: Bid to withhold MI5 information from Heaton Park attack inquests - BBC News Image source, Family handouts Image caption, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, were killed in the attack on the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester Published 3 September 2026 The Government has applied to block some MI5 information relating to the fatal Manchester synagogue attack from being heard in public, a court has heard. A pre-inquest hearing at Manchester Coroner's Court was told the Home Office wanted the information to be withheld when the inquests into the deaths of Adrian Daulby, 53, and Melvin Cravitz, 66, are held next year. Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in Manchester on 2 October last year. He then began attacking with a knife, while wearing a fake suicide belt. Cravitz died from multiple knife wounds while Daulby was killed by a bullet fired by armed police scrambled to the scene. He was hit as he blocked the synagogue doors to stop Al-Shamie getting in. The hearing earlier was told by Neil Sheldon KC, representing the Home Office, that making public the information held by MI5 would put national security at risk. He said: "The Secretary of State asserts that disclosure would harm national security." But lawyers for the families of the victims said the Government's attempt to withhold the information, through a Public Interest Immunity application, was in "contradiction" to statements made after the attack. The family lawyers cited statements made by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood and counter-terror police bosses that terrorist Al-Shamie was not on their radar and unknown to them. Victoria Ailes, representing the Cravitz family, told Judge Alexia Durran, Chief Coroner of England and Wales: "We would respectfully suggest the interest in open justice is heightened." Anna Morris KC, representing the Daulby family, said there had been a "demonstrable lack of candour" by the security services in "other proceedings". She said the Daulby family were also concerned that this application and information might contradict statements made publicly that the terrorist was not known to counter terror policing or the security services. The Daulby family expected a "rigorous investigation" into his death and the family had concerns about any delay in proceedings and "procedural rights", she added. Image caption, A decision on whether Yoni Finlay, injured by the same bullet that killed Daulby, should be an "interested party" was deferred by the coroner to the next hearing Ed Pleeth, counsel to the inquest, told the hearing the PII application by the Home Office showed a "well-evidenced" risk to national security but the MI5 information was also relevant to the inquests that must take place. He said in inquests there is no power to exclude certain parties, such as lawyers representing families or other parties, so the MI5 material could then not be heard. Pleeth said the coroner must consider whether to convert the inquests into a public inquiry, where the law does allow sensitive security information to be examined in "closed" or private hearings attended only by a senior judge and security vetted lawyers. Due to the "procedural uncertainty", no date has yet been set for the next pre-inquest hearing and a written ruling on the PII application is expected from the Chief Coroner at a later date. Earlier, the Chief Coroner granted "interested person" status, meaning they will be legally represented at either the inquest or public inquiry, to three Greater Manchester Police firearms officers called to the scene, identified only as F42, S19 and C25. The hearing was told officer F42 fired four times from his Glock pistol, with his first shot missing Al-Shamie and fatally hitting Daulby and injuring a second man, Yoni Finlay. Officer S19 fired five times and C25 once, both using a "carbine" weapon. Andrew Franks, who the court heard opened the synagogue compound gates to Al-Shamie, was also given interested person status, but the coroner said this did not imply any "criticism or culpability" on his behalf. candidates.title: Union secures £15k towards unpaid Manchester Pride performer fees
candidates.summary: The performers went unpaid after the charity previously running Manchester Pride went bust in 2025
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The performers went unpaid after the charity previously running Manchester Pride went bust in 2025
candidates.evidence_text: Union secures £15k towards unpaid Manchester Pride performer fees - BBC News Image caption, Performers' union Equity says its unpaid members were "the heart of Manchester Pride" By Angela Ferguson North West Published 3 September 2026 A trade union representing some of the performers left unpaid after the charity running Manchester Pride went into administration said it has managed to secure £15,000. Equity said the money came from contributions from businesses within the "social action pot" put forward by Manchester City Council. It comes amid an ongoing Charity Commission investigation into the organisation which previously ran the event. Equity member and LGBTQ+ theatre-maker and activist Nathaniel Hall said it was "encouraging" news and, while the money would not cover all the losses, "the gesture is really welcome". Hall said LGBTQ+ Equity members "can be proud they have a union that has their backs when times are tough". The charity previously behind Manchester Pride entered voluntary liquidation in October 2025 . In a statement issued on 12 August, the Charity Commission said they were continuing to liaise with liquidators regarding Manchester Pride and their regulatory compliance case into the charity was ongoing. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, People have gathered in Manchester for the annual pride event for more than 40 years after its humble beginnings in 1985 Equity said it was contacting more than 50 performers who came forward to say they were owed £70,000. It said it would be distributing a percentage of unpaid fees to each artist, equating to about 20% of what they were owed. They said the funding, coupled with a £12,500 crowdfund sum organised by Nathaniel Hall brought the total raised to £27,500, almost 40% of the money owed. Equity North West official Karen Lockney said it was "great news for the many performers who were left high and dry last year when Manchester Pride went bust". Lockney added that they were grateful to the council and all those who donated. Council leader Garry Bridges said the authority was pleased to have been able to work with Equity "to find a meaningful way to help those worst affected without using public money to meet the debts of a failed business". But Belinda Scandal said she was concerned about drag artists such as herself and a number of others who were still awaiting payment but could not afford to pay Equity membership fees. "I'd just like to know how that money is going to be divvied out now they have got it and if it's just going to be Equity members," she said. Scandal said she had got £370 out of £2,500 owed to her so far but she needed more to pay the other performers who worked with her. She praised the organisers of this year's event, however, saying performers had already been paid on time. candidates.evidence_text: A mother has told how her family's lives changed overnight when her son developed life-threatening sepsis at the age of five Archie, from Wigan, Greater Manchester, was diagnosed with meningitis B which developed into sepsis , external and he spent five days in a coma in 2018 He was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, where he received specialist care and rehabilitation before being discharged two weeks later His mother Kate said her son's illness "changed our lives overnight" and seeing him "so seriously unwell and fighting for his life was the most frightening time we have ever experienced as a family" Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to infection anywhere in the body, where, instead of fighting the bacteria or virus that is making you ill, the immune system turns on itself, damaging internal organs and potentially causing death Now aged 13, Archie continues to receive care at the hospital, attending for regular check-ups, undergoing operations, and receiving physiotherapy and occupational therapy

candidates.title: Production at Kellogg's Trafford Park factory comes to an end
candidates.summary: The factory was built in 1938 and once produced a million boxes of cereal a day
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The factory was built in 1938 and once produced a million boxes of cereal a day
candidates.evidence_text: Production at Kellogg's Trafford Park factory comes to an end - BBC News Image source, Peter McDermott Image caption, Production is moving to a Kellogg's site in Wrexham in north Wales By Richard Stead , Reporting from in Trafford Park and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 3 September 2026 Production at the Kellogg's factory in Greater Manchester has come to an end after almost 90 years, with the loss of about 360 jobs. The site in Trafford Park was one of the largest cereal factories in Europe when built in 1938 but production is being transferred to the company's site in Wrexham, north Wales. A spokesperson for owners Kellanova said the site has been a crucial part of its success for decades, adding: "We thank everyone who has worked there, as well as the suppliers, partners and local community who have worked alongside us." Mick Murray from retail union Usdaw said it was "a sad time" after working to "try to secure the best possible outcome for our members". In 2024 Kellanova announced that production of breakfast cereals would move to Wrexham, saying the investment required to maintain the factory was not viable. It came after the end of three-month talks with union and employee representatives . Marking the last week of production on site, a company spokesperson said: "A significant milestone was reached this week, as operations across production and packing came to an end." They said their priority through the transition has been to "support colleagues and the wider community through this period of change". Image source, Kellanova Image caption, The Trafford Park site was once one of the largest food manufacturing facilities in Europe Kellogg's is an American company founded in Michigan in 1906. It began exporting to the UK in 1922. The cereal giant said the Trafford Park factory was laid out in a way that made sense in the 1930s, with food travelling up and down six floors in a legacy manufacturing process , the company previously said. The site once produced a million boxes of breakfast cereal a day, including Corn Flakes, Rice Krispies and Coco Pops. The company said half of the space in the Trafford Park building was unused and it would have cost too much to redevelop the site. The site will remain open until the end of the year. Kellanova said it would work with local partners to recognise and celebrate the site's legacy and would also continue to mark special milestones in the months ahead. The firm continues to have a large footprint in the North West, with about 500 jobs remaining at its UK head office at Media City in Salford and at a distribution centre in St Helens. Murray said Usdaw had worked to support members and to secure an enhanced redundancy package along with relocation payments for those who decided to move to Wrexham. He praised the "strong" team of union representatives on the shop floor at the Trafford Park site for their efforts over the years. candidates.summary: Bev Craig says people from across all 10 boroughs had complained to her about potholes

candidates.lead: Bev Craig says people from across all 10 boroughs had complained to her about potholes
candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor launches £60m pothole repair programme - BBC News Image caption, Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig says the funding will be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road By Mairead Smyth , Reporting from in Eccles and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 3 September 2026 The mayor of Greater Manchester has unveiled a £60m pothole repair programme, saying people from all 10 boroughs had complained to her about the issue. Bev Craig said funding would be made available to all of the boroughs and it would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road. Craig had promised to repair more roads and make sure pavements were safe during her election campaign. But Rod Dennis from the RAC said what was needed to fix "Britain's pothole woes, and those we see in Manchester, is guaranteed long-term funding over many, many years". Image caption, Funding is being made available to all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs Dennis called for "an end to the kind of patch and dash approach which we've seen some councils employ and proper planning to get the roads back to where they need to be". Craig said 2.5 billion journeys were made across the roads of Greater Manchester every year "and we need to properly invest in them and this is about getting money out of the door quickly to fix the things that people have been complaining to me about". Image caption, Garage owner Dave Rigby says that almost every day he sees drivers bring in vehicles damaged by potholes Dave Rigby, who runs a garage in Eccles, told BBC North West Tonight that potholes were "quite a big factor", with vehicles often brought in there every day for repairs as a result of them. He said they could damage a vehicle's suspension as well as damaging tyres and wheel alignment and tracking. "From a business point of view, obviously we do make money off it but, for customers, the cost of living's gone up and stuff, so, obviously, if the roads are better it's more money in people's pockets," he said. 'Common and frustrating' Transport for Greater Manchester said the allocated funding would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road, helping to tackle existing issues and resurface roads and pavements to prevent them from deteriorating in the first place. It said damaged sections of roads and pavements were "a common and frustrating issue affecting drivers across the country", as well as walkers and cyclists. The funding is being divided across all 10 boroughs as follows: Bolton - £6.55m Bury - £4.37m Manchester - £8.16m Oldham - £5.26m Rochdale - £5.24m Salford - £5.39m Stockport - £6.82m Tameside - £4.98m Trafford - £4.99m Wigan - £8.24m Craig said these amounts were worked out using a formula "based on how many roads you've got and the length of roads". She said the way it had been shared out across local authorities was simply "the more roads you have, the more money you get". The extra funding comes from existing transport budgets and follows a national increase in government funding for pothole repairs. candidates.lead: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
candidates.evidence_text: Six serving police officers have been sacked following an internal investigation by Greater Manchester Police into alleged racial discrimination against a fellow officer GMP said two other former officers who were also investigated would have been fired if they were still on the force. Another officer received written warning A force disciplinary panel heard the female officer of African heritage (who was not named in the proceedings) complained after her accent was mimicked by a group of officers She was also compared to a suspect with similar skin colour, while one officer made a derogatory comment about her hair The panel found six officers and two former officers committed gross misconduct, while a ninth officer was found to have committed misconduct PCs Demi Green, Heena Rani, Lucy Granby, Matthew Barlow, Matthew Hill, and Mohammed Abid - who made the remark about his colleague's hair - were dismissed without notice

candidates.evidence_text: An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope" It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City's lease at the Etihad Stadium was placed under review last month amid a major expansion of the club's east Manchester campus, it has emerged City has a long-term lease at the ground with Manchester City Council and finished expanding its north stand earlier this year, which increased the stadium capacity to more than 60,000 people It has been building a new £300m entertainment zone known as Medlock Square which includes a Radisson Blu Hotel and a zip-line, with plans for a new 600-person capacity entertainment venue which the council granted planning permission in June The lease review was sparked as a result of changes taking place around the Etihad Campus, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) understands Council papers describing a decision about a "variation of leases with Manchester City Football Club" have been made public on the town hall's website but specifics of the finances have been kept hidden from view The review is expected to result in an uplift in the yearly base rate fee paid to the city council from the club, currently said to be between £3m to £4m a year

candidates.evidence_text: An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope" It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist

candidates.evidence_text: “A lot of cars park on single yellow or double yellow, and people don’t understand why they’re getting a ticket, they’ll plead with you just to give them one more minute. It can be very difficult,” he told my colleague Declan Carey, who visited the stretch this week While there Declan heard car horns blaring, pedestrians veering wildly into the road and plenty of road rage. Dubbed Manchester’s ‘worst’ road, many shopkeepers told Declan they’ve seen accidents and deaths on the ‘horrendous’ road since the 1990s “It’s one of the worst roads in Manchester, it’s total chaos in the evenings,” the traffic warden adds View 6 Images Traffic chaos Stockport Road in Longsight. Picture Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News) Data kept by Transport for Greater Manchester points to a major safety problem on Stockport Road. A fatality happened in 2025 at the ever-busy junction with Slade Lane Further up by Stanley Road and Dickenson Road, the area is littered with accident reports, with multiple minor and serious collisions logged since 2024. But can anything really be done to improve things?

candidates.evidence_text: Cheshire Police Cheshire detective whose secret actions were 'beyond belief' is barred from policing forever The cop at Cheshire Police has been dismissed for gross misconduct Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:03, 04 Sep 2026 View Image A detective who looked up information about a suspect being investigated by someone else and then trying to prevent criminal charges has been sacked for gross misconduct The detective inspector at Cheshire Police, whose name and gender have been kept secret, was sacked by the force's chief constable, Mark Roberts, following a misconduct hearing last month The unnamed officer involved themselves in an investigation which had nothing to do with them where they knew the family of the suspect and creating a 'conflict of interest', according to a published ruling The DI was said to have kept their relationship with the family secret from colleagues and then 'attempted to influence the investigation and outcome' in February 2026 The officer emailed the mother of the suspect and accessed police computer systems for information about the case 'without a legitimate policing purpose'

They had no prior relationship, it was said The woman asked her to come back when her children weren't home but just hours later Huo continued banging on the door with her keys and shouted: "Your dad is a paedophile, he sexually abuses kids. Your dad is a judge." Following further visits to the woman's home demanding money, Huo then sent a letter to the other neighbours in the area, about the woman. It read: "Dear neighbour, they [at house number] are paedophiles.... Her father is a judge... Please keep your children safe. From your frien Manchester Crown Court heard that days later the woman woke to sounds of smashing glass. Ella Worsley , prosecuting, said: "She looked out the window and saw the defendant hitting the rear window of her car with a hammer

candidates.evidence_text: Politics Angela Rayner to set up antisemitism committee amid spate of hate crimes against Jewish community "Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety" News Sophie W A Cabinet committee on antisemitism will be set up to address concerns over a spate of hate crimes against the Jewish community, Angela Rayner has announced The plan was unveiled by the Housing, Communities and Local Government Secretary today (September 3) during a roundtable in Downing Street with leaders from the community. The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham acknowledged “how much the community is struggling” He told the gathering: “Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety.” Leaders of Jewish organisations told the Prime Minister and Ms Rayner that measures were needed to address the community’s heightened fears heading into the Jewish holiday season, a year on from the Manchester synagogue terror attack Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the synagogue on October 2 2025 and began attacking with a knife while wearing a fake suicide belt

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Metropolitan University Manchester Metropolitan University accused of 'pure hypocrisy' over land row The university has come under fire from a councillor about its plans for Ryebank Fields Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter Manchester Metropolitan University (MMU) has been accused of ‘pure hypocrisy’ in a row over its plans to flog Ryebank Fields in Chorlton for developers to build new homes Chantal Kerr-Sheppard, a Green Party councillor in Chorlton, said MMU promoted a ‘biodiversity’ campaign in May called Make a Metre Matter, which encouraged people to ‘plant and [make] green spaces’, while at the same time pressing ahead with its own plans to sell off a large pat A planning application led by MMU along with Step Places and Southway Housing Trust is aiming to build 120 homes on Ryebank Fields. If approved, the job would involve work to fix the land’s ‘contamination with asbestos, heavy metals and hazardous hydrocarbons’, MMU said Councillor Kerr-Sheppard said the planning reports to build homes on Ryebank Fields, which are published online and have been seen by the Local Democracy Reporting Service, showed it would mean a ‘40 per cent net loss in biodiversity’ for animal habitats in the area The planning reports also showed the application to build on the land would need ‘offsite mitigation’ to make up for the changes

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at Bolton town hall as a debate about creating a more ‘respectful’ political atmosphere in the town descended into 'screaming in and playground behaviour' Following the unsavoury meeting, one councillor said ‘the people of Bolton watching this will be appalled’ as voices were raised and the mayor, Mohammed Iqbal, called for order several times Angry exchanges came during the debate about rising ‘hostility, abuse and intimidation towards elected members’, with a pledge made by all parties to support the Local Government Association’s ‘Debate Not Hate’ initiative Towards the end of the debate, as Jackie Schofield, a Labour councillor, was starting her speech, shouting could be heard between the Reform UK and Labour benches, prompted by an earlier reference to the Makerfield by-election Coun Schofield said: “I feel like I’m in a school playground, you really need to grow up. You really need to think about why you’re here and why you were elected to this role. The people of Bolton watching this will be appalled. That’s everybody, across every party.”

About 800 barrels of the stout, estimated to be worth around £115,000, were taken from an industrial estate in Runcorn on Monday, Cheshire Constabulary has revealed. They were o The force said it was hoping for a 'full recovery of the stolen items' and has appealed for witnesses who may have seen a lorry entering the Aston Lane area at about 7.45pm The lorry is said to have connected to an HGV trailer containing the Guinness and left the site at about 7.55pm in the direction of the Mersey Gateway bridge A second lorry arrived at the same site at 9.12pm and connected to another trailer, which also contained barrels of Guinness, before leaving at 9.30pm in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way, police said The stolen barrels, containing around 70,400 pints of the Irish tipple, had been intended to be delivered to pubs

Police shared the footage, which was captured just before 7pm Alongside the clip, a GMP spokesperson wrote: "Last night (Wednesday 2 September 2026) some Lamborghini drivers thought they were on an episode of Drive to Survive. Spoiler alert: they weren't "Our new Transport Policing and Crime Command team helped bring them back to reality, seizing five Lamborghinis and a Mercedes G-Wagon, after reports of dangerous driving. The only pitstop they are making is to the vehicle impound." The high-powered cars were first spotted speeding on the M66 motorway last night. The cars were seen weaving across lanes, wheel spinning and slowing down to speeds of around 17mph on the motorway, police said The vehicles were then spotted on the M62 , with officers deployed to bring them to a stop. Two Lamborghinis were stopped as they came off the motorway

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Tameside Hospital 'truly sorry' after woman sent home from A&E dies days later 'We are truly sorry', said a spokesperson for Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 05:50, 04 Sep 2026 U A coroner has warned that more patients could be at risk of dying at Tameside Hospital after an 87-year-old woman was sent home from the emergency department, despite abnormal blood results Judith Marsland died from sepsis days after she visited Tameside General Hospital with abdominal pain and bleeding. A Prevention of Future Deaths report has raised concerns about the care the 87-year old received and warned that action is needed to prevent further deaths A spokesperson from Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care, which runs Tameside Hospital, said the Trust is "truly sorry" that the patient did not receive an adequate standard of care. They said the hospital is "continuing to implement actions" to reduce the risk of similar inciden Mrs Marsland, from Tameside, died in hospital on November 14, 2025, after developing sepsis from a urinary tract infection a coroner said was likely already present when she attended A&E eight days earlier According to a coroner’s report, sepsis was considered by medics while Mrs Marsland was in the emergency department, but she was not managed on a sepsis pathway

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council tried to hold a meeting about 'respect', it did not go well 'The people of Bolton will be appalled' Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 18:06, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 21:40, 03 Sep 2026 View 2 Images The meeting took pla There were heated scenes at Bolton town hall as a debate about creating a more ‘respectful’ political atmosphere in the town descended into 'screaming in and playground behaviour' Following the unsavoury meeting, one councillor said ‘the people of Bolton watching this will be appalled’ as voices were raised and the mayor, Mohammed Iqbal, called for order several times Angry exchanges came during the debate about rising ‘hostility, abuse and intimidation towards elected members’, with a pledge made by all parties to support the Local Government Association’s ‘Debate Not Hate’ initiative Towards the end of the debate, as Jackie Schofield, a Labour councillor, was starting her speech, shouting could be heard between the Reform UK and Labour benches, prompted by an earlier reference to the Makerfield by-election Coun Schofield said: “I feel like I’m in a school playground, you really need to grow up. You really need to think about why you’re here and why you were elected to this role. The people of Bolton watching this will be appalled. That’s everybody, across every party.”

candidates.evidence_text: Politics Angela Rayner to set up antisemitism committee amid spate of hate crimes against Jewish community "Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety" News Sophie W A Cabinet committee on antisemitism will be set up to address concerns over a spate of hate crimes against the Jewish community, Angela Rayner has announced The plan was unveiled by the Housing, Communities and Local Government Secretary today (September 3) during a roundtable in Downing Street with leaders from the community. The Prime Minister, Andy Burnham acknowledged “how much the community is struggling” He told the gathering: “Right now, the levels of anxiety are really quite high and probably never higher in terms of a sense of people’s personal safety.” Leaders of Jewish organisations told the Prime Minister and Ms Rayner that measures were needed to address the community’s heightened fears heading into the Jewish holiday season, a year on from the Manchester synagogue terror attack Melvin Cravitz, 66, and Adrian Daulby, 53, were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of the synagogue on October 2 2025 and began attacking with a knife while wearing a fake suicide belt

Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face The complainants are referred to as Girl A, Girl B and Girl C for legal reasons. Earlier in the trial, prosecutor Rossano Scamardella KC claimed that Mr Rashid began 'buying her presents and even gave her money’

candidates.evidence_text: “A lot of cars park on single yellow or double yellow, and people don’t understand why they’re getting a ticket, they’ll plead with you just to give them one more minute. It can be very difficult,” he told my colleague Declan Carey, who visited the stretch this week While there Declan heard car horns blaring, pedestrians veering wildly into the road and plenty of road rage. Dubbed Manchester’s ‘worst’ road, many shopkeepers told Declan they’ve seen accidents and deaths on the ‘horrendous’ road since the 1990s “It’s one of the worst roads in Manchester, it’s total chaos in the evenings,” the traffic warden adds View 6 Images Traffic chaos Stockport Road in Longsight. Picture Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News) Data kept by Transport for Greater Manchester points to a major safety problem on Stockport Road. A fatality happened in 2025 at the ever-busy junction with Slade Lane Further up by Stanley Road and Dickenson Road, the area is littered with accident reports, with multiple minor and serious collisions logged since 2024. But can anything really be done to improve things?

The cars were a black Dacia Duster, a red Kia Niro and a black Ford Focu Sadly, 38-year-old Krisstoffer, known as Kriss, died on the scene. candidates.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.evidence_text: Today Simple Minds’ announce details of their brand new studio album, Sacrosanct, to be released on 29 January 2027 on BMG and they will playing at Manchester’s Co-op Live next May In the four years since 2022’s top 5 album Direction Of The Heart, the band have been busier than ever, releasing a critically acclaimed career spanning documentary, publishing a joint memoir (Uncut magazine and Rough Trade’s ‘Books of The Year’), and delivering live shows across Last year alone they played in front of over 1.5m people and some of their biggest audiences since 1985, on their hugely successful Global Tour. Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

candidates.source_evidence: Cllr Garry Bridges is set to be appointed as the new Leader of Manchester City Council at a special meeting this week (Thursday 3 September, 6pm) Cllr Bridges succeeds Cllr Bev Craig, who was elected as Greater Manchester Mayor in July, having previously served as statutory Deputy Leader since 2024. Subject to confirmation at the full Council meeting, he will take up the political leadership of the Council The Leader has ultimate responsibility for setting the long-term vision for the Council at the heart of Manchester’s ongoing inclusive growth, leading a team of Executive (Cabinet) members. He will represent the Council – and the city – at regional, national and international lev Cllr Bridges’ political priority has been ensuring that Manchester’s young people have the best start in life and have the opportunities, through work and skills, to share in the city’s success Prior to becoming Deputy Leader in 2024, Cllr Bridges had held the position of Executive Member for Children and Schools and overseen significant improvements across children’s services – which are now rated Outstanding by Ofsted. This included championing free school meals durin His commitment has been accentuated by his role as a parent to two toddlers, a daughter (aged three) and a son (aged four.)

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham’s Halloween Half Marathon, the borough's gruelling 13.1 mile race, is back Taking place on Sunday 25 October, the event offers a rewarding challenge for any runner. Its hilly course – considered by many to be the toughest in the country – is guaranteed to get your heart racing and blood pumping Whether you are looking for a new running challenge, you want to raise money for charity, or you’re looking to compete just for fun, anyone aged 17 and over can now sign-up to take part on Oldham Community Leisure’s website Entry fees start from £35, with local running groups and clubs able to enter for just £33 Runners will begin this year’s half marathon on St Mary’s Way in Oldham, before taking a steady incline up to Grains Bar, where at a whopping 340 metres above sea level, the course reaches its infamous peak From here, keen runners will enjoy breathtaking views of the Saddleworth countryside as they make their way through Delph, Dobcross and Uppermill, before heading on to Grasscroft and Lydgate to begin their return leg

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ПАВЕЛ ДЕДИЩЕВ В ЛОНДОНЕ | 30ГО СЕНТЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Wednesday, September 30 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Павел Дедищев выступит в Лондоне со своим стендап концертом "АМЕРИКАНЕЦ" Лондон! 30го сентября к нам приезжает Павел Дедищев со своим концертом "Американец" Резидент шоу Stand Up на ТНТ, финалист «Comedy Баттл» и «Большого шоу», участник проектов «Решалы» и «Было слово». Он стоял у истоков объединения HIT2SHIT (будущего Labelcom), стал сооснователем канала «Комьюнити» и одним из тех, кто формировал новую волну русскоязычного стендапа. Павел Дедищев - комик с ярко выраженным собственным стилем, в котором сочетаются честность, дерзость и умение подмечать детали, знакомые каждому. Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. Дедищев говорит прямо, не сглаживает углы и именно этим вызывает у зрителей тот самый взрывной смех. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:45 End: 21:30 Мы работаем по принципу first come, first served, а именно, кто пришел раньше, то и занял лучшее место. 18+ P.S. candidates.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. It should mean earlier engagement

candidates.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

candidates.evidence_text: BGF-backed Celerity makes second acquisition in 6 months Posted on September 3, 2026 by staff BGF-backed Celerity makes second acquisition in 6 months Manchester-based IT services firm which swooped for Ranger4 in April now moves for Warwick business Insight 2 Value Share: Deals Celerity, a Manchester-based managed IT services provider backed by investor BGF, has acquired Insight 2 Value (I2V). Based in Warwick, I2V is a specialist in intelligent automation and enterprise content management, with expertise in IBM FileNet and Cloud Pak for business automation. The acquisition will strengthen Celerity’s capacity to provide solutions that improve customer onboarding, complaints handling, case management and regulatory compliance, connecting content seamlessly to improve service delivery and accelerate customer-facing operations. “We’re thrilled to welcome Insight 2 Value to our team. This acquisition means our customers can now benefit from even more powerful solutions – combining intelligent automation and content-driven workflows with our cyber-resilient infrastructure,” said Craig Aston, CEO of Celerity. “Together, we can help organisations streamline their most critical processes, reduce complexity, and ultimately deliver better experiences to their own customers. “This is about giving our customers access to smarter, more integrated tools that tackle the challenges that matter most to your business.” Phil Hagen, managing director of Insight 2 Value, said: “Joining Celerity is a natural next step for Insight 2 Value. We’ve dedicated ourselves to helping businesses simplify experiences and deliver rapid value while mitigating common implementation challenges. “Celerity gives I2V a platform to continue developing market-leading solutions and delivering exceptional client services for organisations of all sizes, whilst working alongside a wider team of exceptional talent and a service portfolio that complements everything we do.” Edinburgh firm pureLiFi crashes into administration Celerity has achieved accelerated growth since receiving a £15m investment from growth capital investors BGF in 2021, which has helped drive service diversification, strategic partnerships and complementary acquisitions. The transaction follows Celerity’s acquisition of Ranger4 in April 2026, taking the business’ headcount to a team of 107. Harry Jones, partner at BGF, added: “This acquisition is an important milestone for Celerity that will further differentiate its service proposition. candidates.lead: Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities.
candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

City responded with a £125m bid - which Chelsea accepted. Fernandez was amongst several midfielders who switched clubs this summer. Manchester United acquired Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos for a combined £155m

candidates.evidence_text: Music & Nightlife Noel Gallagher confirms summer 2027 for Oasis tour return - as football schedules align The football schedules may be playing a bigger part than Oasis fans realise, as Noel Gallagher confirms that the band are set to fill the void in summer 2027 Commen Noel Gallagher has given the strongest confirmation yet that Oasis are to make a big summer 2027 return to the live music arena. Noel had remained tight-lipped about the new tour rumours in recent months, while brother Liam Gallagher has been teasing fans with lots of hints and c However now, in his own words, Noel has confirmed there's "something happening" in summer 2027. Speaking to TalkSport presenter Andy Goldstein on Wednesday night, there was plenty of banter about brother Liam's recent departure from social media site X Liam had urged Noel on X to announce a new tour, saying: "Ffs RKID announce the tour we’re all losing our minds." He then went on to say he was quitting social media amid apparent frustrations about the "goose chases" around the new tour rumours As the MEN revealed earlier this summer , the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, home to the Gallaghers' beloved Manchester City, is set to host up to 12 gigs from Oasis across June 2027. Man City's games conclude at the end of May, giving Oasis free reign to take over the ground for The MEN understands from music industry sources that the gig schedule will see three gigs a week, including weekends, at the Etihad Stadium across June, while plans are also afoot to stage a huge return to Knebworth from the band later in the summer
